newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sends cargo load of wheat to Mexico by US rail.
newsitem.headline: CWB sends cargo load of wheat to Mexico by US rail.

text.p: The equivalent of an ocean vessel load of Canadian milling wheat is currently being railed through the United States to a Mexican client, a Canadian Wheat Board spokesman said.
"We're sending a milling wheat cargo by rail south in view of our transportation problems on the East coast and West coast," CWB chief of communications Bob Roehle told Reuters.
The wheat is being carried in hopper cars and locomotives owned by Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp, he said.
"It's happening right now," Roehle added. He declined to disclose tonnage and dollar value.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure lead to delays in rail shipments to Pacific ports since early January.
Canadian Wheat Board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines and admitted to deferring sales.
There were seven vessels loading Canadian grain at Pacific port Tuesday and 33 waiting, one as long as 46 days, CWB said.
The Pacific port backlog has seen the CWB ship more than 80,000 tonnes of grain to Portland or Gulf terminals since early January, the CWB said.
The CWB railed Canadian grain through the U.S. was due to a Pacific port strike in March, 1995, the CWB has said.
The only other time was when the CWB railed a small durum wheat shipment to Latin America in July 1996, CWB has said.
On the East coast, shipments through Thunder Bay were not possible as the harbour remains closed until after the St. Lawrence Seaway opens April 2 once the winter ice breaks up.
Meanwhile, east-bound grain is railed to the St. Lawrence River.
Mexican wheat buyers can take delivery of Canadian milling wheat either on their east or west coasts, Roehle said.
